Hi Olivia — quick technical notes and recommended POC integration approach. TL;DR: we expose both a dedicated rerank API and model-parameter-based reranking; for clarity/simplicity start with POST /v1/rerank (hosted) and top_k tuning as outlined below.

Auth & SDKs:
- Hosted: API Key header (Authorization: Bearer <KEY>) via our SDKs (python/node/java) or curl.
- Private/Dedicated: support for mTLS and customer-managed KMS for key wrapping; RBAC and VPC peering available on request.

Endpoint options:
1) Dedicated rerank endpoint (recommended for POC): POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/rerank
   - Body: {"query": "...", "candidates": ["...","..."], "top_k": 50, "return_metadata": true}
   - Response: array of {"candidate_id": "...", "score": 0.87, "explain": "matched title and brand"}
2) Inline rerank parameter on search/generate call (useful if you already use a single endpoint for other features).

Top_k and cost/latency tradeoffs:
- We commonly recommend a two-stage flow: candidate generation (your retrieval -> ~200–500 candidates) followed by a rerank pass with top_k set to a smaller value if you do heavy rescoring, or full rerank of all candidates if latency budget allows.
- Example approach: retrieve 500 -> coarse embed-score to filter to 100 -> rerank top 100 -> return top 10 to UI.
- For hosted models, expect roughly linear cost/latency with top_k; reranking 100 candidates typically adds ~80–120ms median on a GPU-optimized runtime (varies by model size/quantization).

Structured output / explainability:
- return_metadata / tool-calling: set return_metadata=true to receive structured explain fields per candidate. We can also support a JSON schema (structured output) so your frontend can surface signals (matched fields, confidence bands).

Embeddings vs reranker:
- Embeddings are great for candidate generation and coarse filtering (cheap, scalable); learned rerankers (cross-encoders) provide better final ranking accuracy at higher cost. Typical pattern is hybrid: embedders for retrieval, reranker for final ordering and feature combination.

SDK snippet (python):

import requests
url = "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/rerank"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
payload = {"query": "running shoes men size 10", "candidates": ["c1","c2","c3"], "top_k": 100, "return_metadata": True}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(resp.json())

Notes on batching and throughput:
- Use concurrent batching for high QPS; prefer our SDK batch_rerank helper which will manage chunking and backpressure.
- Cache prefix scores for repeated queries; set TTLs based on traffic patterns.

Hi Olivia/Marissa — some recommended evaluation and significance guidance for the POC.

Primary metrics:
- NDCG@10 / NDCG@20: captures graded relevance and position bias.
- Precision@k (k=1,3,5,10): easy-to-interpret business metric for top results.
- MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank): useful if you expect one relevant item per query.
- Recall@k: important if downstream reranker or business needs to ensure relevant items are surfaced at all.

Secondary and qualitative:
- Calibration of score -> human judgment (get 200–500 labeled queries for a sanity check).
- CTR and downstream conversion lift during live A/B (if you can run an experiment).

Labeling guidance / sample size:
- For initial offline evaluation, 1,000–2,000 labeled queries with 5–10 candidate labels each gives reasonably stable NDCG estimates; smaller pilots (300–500) can surface large wins but may be noisy.
- Use graded labels (0 = not relevant, 1 = somewhat, 2 = highly relevant) to compute NDCG.
- Randomly split queries for training/tuning vs validation; hold out 20% for final evaluation.

Top_k tuning suggestion:
- Start: retrieve 500 -> embed filter to 100 -> rerank top 100 and return top 10. Tune top_k on validation set by plotting NDCG@10 vs. cost/latency. Often gains plateau beyond reranking 150–200 candidates.

A/B plan for production:
- 2-week experiment, target 50–100k queries per arm for reliable online metrics (CTR/Conversion). If you can’t run that many, focus on offline metrics + smaller live tests for inferred impact.

If helpful, we can provide a simple evaluation harness and baseline scripts to compute NDCG/MRR from labeled CSVs. I can prep that and share in the repo.
